text_blocks.snippet: Vulvar cancer is a rare cancer that occurs on the external female genitalia, the vulva. It typically develops slowly over several years, with precancerous changes often preceding the development of cancer. Common symptoms include persistent itching, pain, or a noticeable lump on the vulva.
snippet_highlighted_words: Vulvar cancer is a rare cancer that occurs on the external female genitalia, the vulva

list.title: Types:
list.snippet: The most common type is squamous cell carcinoma, which can be linked to HPV infection or chronic inflammation. Other types include adenocarcinoma (often originating in Bartholin or sweat glands) and melanoma.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Early-stage vulvar cancer may not cause noticeable symptoms, but as it progresses, symptoms can include:
Itching, burning, or soreness of the vulva
A lump, swelling, or wart-like growth on the vulva
Thickened, raised, red, white, or dark patches on the skin
Bleeding or discharge not related to menstruation

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: Factors that may increase the risk of vulvar cancer include HPV infection, lichen sclerosus, and a history of vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN).

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Diagnosis often involves a biopsy of any suspicious areas on the vulva, along with imaging and other tests to assess the extent of the cancer.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment options vary depending on the stage and type of cancer, but may include surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, or a combination of these.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: If you experience any persistent or concerning symptoms in the vulvar area, it's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.
